_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. status: active = connector-only, a reprint would clobber it; upstreamed = also fixed in the press, a reprint from a fixed press regenerates it, but the back-port must still be present today.

handfixes.summary: `n-central-mcp` accepts --transport/--addr and PP_MCP_TRANSPORT, matching the 58 connectors that already do
handfixes.why: main() called server.ServeStdio unconditionally and never parsed os.Args, so `n-central-mcp --transport http` was silently ignored and the process still served stdio. Four of the six affected connectors ship an mcp-install.md instructing users to pass exactly that flag, so the documentation described a mode the binary did not have. The block added here is copied verbatim from the generated shape the other 58 connectors already carry (see skills/halopsa/cli/cmd/halopsa-mcp/main.go): a --transport flag defaulting to defaultTransport(), which reads PP_MCP_TRANSPORT and falls back to stdio so no-argument invocation is unchanged, an --addr flag defaulting to :7777, and a switch that serves stdio, serves NewStreamableHTTPServer for http, or exits 2 on an unknown value. This is press drift rather than staleness: cork and avanan are on a NEWER press than several connectors that already have the flag, so a reprint at the current press will not reliably restore it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Make the transport flag block unconditional in the cli-printing-press MCP main template so every future print carries it, and add a generator check that fails when an mcp-install.md documents a flag the printed main.go does not parse (filed as a retro item against the generator).
